findings.description: The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest, unlike audit_trail which does define one.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket, leaving it subject to provider/account defaults and lacking explicit enforcement of private access, increasing risk of accidental public exposure.
This bucket stores ledger export (financial) data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational details or credentials) is stored unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption at rest for object
findings.description: The uploaded object does not specify server_side_encryption/kms_key_id, and it is placed in reports_archive, a bucket that itself lacks default encryption, so this file (vendor roster data, potentially containing PII) is stored unencrypted at rest.
